headline: Airbnb Cracks Down on Unreasonable Guest Tasks
meta_description: Airbnb has updated its policies to protect guests from excessive chores, banning hosts from requiring bed-stripping and dishwashing despite cleaning fees.
summary_short: Airbnb now limits what hosts can ask guests to do, banning tasks like washing dishes and stripping beds—ending years of guest complaints about unreasonable demands.
body:
For years, guests booking accommodations through Airbnb have found themselves facing unexpected chores at checkout—vacuuming, scrubbing dishes, even stripping bedsheets—despite having already paid cleaning fees. Now the platform is putting an end to these practices. Starting with reservations booked on or after 20 November, Airbnb has overhauled its house rules to protect guests from onerous requests that would typically fall to professional cleaners. The company has restricted hosts to seven standard house rules plus other "reasonable" requests, explicitly prohibiting tasks that "require significant effort or time," including stripping beds, taking trash offsite, or washing and putting away dishes.

The updated policy addresses what Airbnb describes as confusion and frustration within its community. "House rules help guests understand what hosts expect, but we've heard from our community that they can be confusing, onerous and hard to manage," the company explained. The new rules will now appear more prominently in reservation reminders, giving guests clearer visibility before they book. While hosts retain control over their properties and can appeal if a request is flagged as non-compliant, they can no longer impose fines on guests.

The timing of this change reflects growing tension on the platform, recently amplified by viral TikTok videos from Georgia-based Airbnb hosts who have gained attention for their stringent property inspections and exacting standards. Their detailed scrutiny—including complaints about misplaced television remotes—sparked both criticism and parody content from other creators, highlighting just how far some hosts had pushed their expectations. Airbnb's new framework acknowledges that while exceptions may apply in specific circumstances, such as water conservation during droughts, the days of treating guests like unpaid housekeeping staff are over.
quick_facts: New rules apply to reservations booked from 20 November onwards
Hosts limited to seven standard house rules plus reasonable requests
Banned tasks: stripping beds, washing dishes, taking trash offsite
Guests already pay cleaning fees for professional services
House rules now displayed prominently in reservation reminders
